name: HP_0034662

name: HP_0034660

name: HP_0034663

name: HP_0004601

name: HP_0006802
label: Abnormal anterior horn cell morphology

name: HP_0007267

name: HP_0007260

definition: A form of lissencephaly characterized by an uneven cortical surface with a so called 'cobblestone' appearace. There are no distinguishable cortical layers.

name: HP_0007263

definition: Atrophy affecting the cerebellum and the spinocerebellar tracts of the spinal cord.

name: HP_0007269

definition: Muscular weakness and atrophy related to loss of the motor neurons of the spinal cord and brainstem.

name: HP_0007262

name: HP_0007265

name: HP_0007266

definition: Defective structure and function of myelin sheaths of the white matter of the brain.

name: HP_0009892

definition: Complete absence of any auricular structures.|Complete absence of the auricle (external ear). The skin of the cheek passes smoothly over the aural area without definite elevation or depression.

name: HP_0009894

name: HP_0009898

definition: Developmental hypoplasia of the crus of the helix. That is, flatter and/or shorter crus helix than average.

name: HP_0009890
label: High anterior hairline
definition: Distance between the hairline (trichion) and the glabella (the most prominent point on the frontal bone above the root of the nose), in the midline, more than two SD above the mean. Alternatively, an apparently increased distance between the hairline and the glabella.|This feature gives the appearance of a tall forehead, and may or may not include reduction of hair in the temporal areas. name: HP_0009895

name: HP_0009891

definition: Flatness of the supraorbital portion of the frontal bones.

name: HP_0009893

definition: The presence of telangiectasia of the ear.

name: HP_0009896
label: Abnormal antitragus morphology
definition: An abnormality of the antitragus, which is a small tubercle opposite to the tragus of the ear. The antitragus and the tragus are separated by the intertragic notch.

name: HP_0009897
label: Horizontal crus of helix
definition: An abnormal horizontal axis orientation of the crus of the helix. That is, the main axis of the crus of the helix is perpendicular to the medial longitudinal axis of the ear, instead of sloping inferoposteriorly.|The term 'railroad track sign' has been used to describe prominent horizontal crus of the helix in combination with prominent and parallel inferior crus of the antihelix. name: HP_0009899
label: Prominent crus of helix
definition: The presence of an abnormally prominent of the crus of the helix. That is, development of the crus helix to the same degree as an average antihelix stem or helix.

name: HP_0040007
label: Absent pigmentation of chest

name: HP_0040009
label: Hyperparakeratosis

name: HP_5200207
label: Inattentiveness illusion
definition: Instances in which individuals fail to perceive or notice salient or significant stimuli in their visual field due to a lack of attention.

name: HP_5200203
label: Proprioceptive hallucination
definition: A type of hallucination that involves the perception of distorted or abnormal sensations related to one's body position or movement.

name: HP_5200205
label: Illusions
definition: Perceptual experiences that involve misinterpretations or distortions of sensory stimuli.

name: HP_5200200
label: Olfactory hallucination
definition: Perception of smell without olfactory stimulus.

name: HP_5200201
label: Gustatory hallucination
definition: Perception of taste without gustatory stimulus.

name: HP_5200208
label: Illusions due to affect
definition: Perceptual distortions or misinterpretations of sensory information arise as a result of the individual's emotional or affective state.

name: HP_5200204
label: Disturbed perception with a stimulus
definition: A perceptual experience in which an individual's perception of sensory stimuli is altered or disrupted in some way, resulting in abnormal or distorted sensory perceptions despite the presence of actual external stimuli.

name: HP_5200202
label: Abnormal interpretation of external stimuli
definition: Abnormal perception of reality is characterized by an abnormal or inaccurate experience of external stimuli.

name: HP_5200209
label: Pareidolia
definition: Apophenia is a psychological phenomenon in which individuals perceive familiar patterns or meaningful images in random or ambiguous stimuli, such as clouds, shadows, or inanimate objects.

name: HP_0003831

definition: Description of conditions in which age of onset is typically later in life and in which penetrance is dependent on the age of the subject.

name: HP_0003835
label: Shoulder subluxation

name: HP_0003834

definition: A displacement or misalignment of the humerus with respect to the other bones of the should joint. Note that a subluxation is a partial dislocation.

name: HP_0003837

name: HP_0034507

definition: An abnormal lesion or swelling seen on gallbladder imaging.

name: HP_0034500

definition: A fracture of the glenoid fossa, a relatively shallow dish is located on the lateral scapula and is the socket portion of the shoulder joint that meets to articulate the humeral head.

name: HP_0034508
label: Fingerprint bodies
definition: Fingerprint bodies are inclusion bodies located at the periphery of the muscle fibers underneath the sarcolemma (subsarcolemmal), consisting of non-membrane-bound packed lamellae arranged in concentric patterns resembling fingerprints.|See Figure 2 of PMID:32008911.

name: HP_0034509
label: Spheroid bodies
definition: An accumulation of myofilamentous material within individual muscle fibers, forming usually round but occasionally elongated bodies ranging from 2 to 15 pm in size. The so-called spheroid bodies stain green with the modified trichrome preparation and are mainly present in the periphery of type 1 muscle fibers, where they may occupy large sectors sharply demarcated from the remainder of the cross-sectioned muscle fiber.|See Figure 3 of PMID:571956.

name: HP_0034505
label: Gallbladder wall thickening
definition: Abnormal increased in the thickness of the wall of the gallbladder.|Gallbladder wall thickening is a common yet nonspecific finding that can occur in a wide range of gallbladder diseases and extracholecystic conditions.

name: HP_0034501
label: Widened mediastinum
definition: Abnormal increase in the width of the mediastinum, often defined as being greater than 6 to 8 cm.|This feature can be ascertained by plain chest radiography. name: HP_0034502
label: Narrow mediastinum
definition: Abnormal decrease in the width of the mediastinum.

name: HP_0034506
label: Gallbladder enlargement
definition: Abnormal increased in the thickness of the size of the gallbladder.

name: HP_0034504
label: Septate gallbladder
definition: Septate gallbladder is characterized by the presence of a septum that divides the gallbladder in two chambers. name: HP_0034503
label: Ovarian torsion
definition: Ovarian torsion is a twisting of the ligaments that support the adnexa, cutting off the blood flow to the ovary.

name: HP_0002722
label: Recurrent abscess formation
definition: An increased susceptibility to abscess formation, as manifested by a medical history of recurrent abscesses.

name: HP_0002721
label: Immunodeficiency
definition: Failure of the immune system to protect the body adequately from infection, due to the absence or insufficiency of some component process or substance.

name: HP_0002729
label: Follicular hyperplasia
definition: Lymphadenopathy (enlargement of lymph nodes) owing to hyperplasia of follicular (germinal) centers.|Lymphadenopathy can be defined as enlargement of lymph nodes. It is just a sign accompanying a great variety of entities with multiple etiologies: acute vs. chronic, benign vs. malignant. One of the most commonly seen histological pictures is lymphadenopathy owing to hyperplasia of follicular (germinal centers) but this one is by far not the only one (See Gaddey HL et al. Unexplained Lymphadenopathy: Evaluation and Differential Diagnosis. Am Fam Physician. 2016 1;94:896-903 and Weiss LM. et al. Benign lymphadenopathies. Mod Pathol. 2013;26 Suppl 1:S88-96).

name: HP_0002723
label: Absence of bactericidal oxidative respiratory burst in phagocytes
definition: An absence of the phase of elevated metabolic activity, during which oxygen consumption increases, that occurs in neutrophils, monocytes, and macrophages shortly after phagocytosing material. An enhanced uptake of oxygen leads to the production, by an NADH dependent system, of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2), superoxide anions and hydroxyl radicals, which play a part in microbiocidal activity.

name: HP_0002728
label: Chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis
definition: Recurrent or persistent superficial Candida infections of the skin, mucous membranes, and nails.|The most commonly involved Candida species is Candida albicans. Chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis (CMC) is usually confined to the cutaneous surface without systemic dissemination. CMC does not represent a specific disease, but rather a phenotypic feature of several immunologic, endocrinologic, and autoimmune disorders.

name: HP_0002726
label: Recurrent Staphylococcus aureus infections
definition: Increased susceptibility to Staphylococcus aureus infections, as manifested by recurrent episodes of Staphylococcus aureus infection.

name: HP_0002724
label: Recurrent Aspergillus infections
definition: An increased susceptibility to Aspergillus infections, as manifested by a history of recurrent episodes of Aspergillus infections.

name: HP_0002725
label: Systemic lupus erythematosus
definition: A chronic, relapsing, inflammatory, and often febrile multisystemic disorder of connective tissue, characterized principally by involvement of the skin, joints, kidneys, and serosal membranes.|This is a bundled term that describes a disease rather than a phenotypic feature, but is left for convenience for annotations of lupus conceived of as a feature of another disease.

name: HP_0002720
label: Decreased circulating IgA level
definition: Decreased levels of immunoglobulin A (IgA).

name: HP_0034050
label: Elevated urinary prostaglandin E2 metabolite level
definition: An increased amount of prostaglandin E2 metabolite (PGE-M) in the urine.|In vivo, PGE2 is rapidly converted to its 13,14-dihydro-15-keto metabolite, with more than 90% of circulating PGE2 cleared by a single passage through the lungs. This metabolite is chemically unstable and undergoes a variable amount of degradation to prostaglandin A (PGA) products. Thus, plasma and urine samples from patients actually contain very little intact PGE2, and the PGE2 metabolites (PGEM) can be measured to provide a more reliable estimate of actual PGE2 production.

name: HP_0034056
label: Increased fecal calprotectin level
definition: An increased amount of calprotectin in the feces.|Calprotectin is a calcium- and zinc-binding protein of the S-100 protein family which is mainly found within neutrophils and throughout the human body. The presence of calprotectin in faeces is a consequence of neutrophil migration into the gastrointestinal tissue due to an inflammatory process. Faecal calprotectin concentrations demonstrate good correlation with intestinal inflammation and faecal calprotectin is used as a biomarker in gastrointestinal disorders.

name: HP_0034058
label: Abnormal fetal morphology
definition: Any structural anomaly of the fetus.

name: HP_0034052
label: Impaired toe-walking ability
definition: Difficulty or reduced ability to walk on toes. Toe-walking can be tested as a part of the neurological examination. Foot plantar flexion weakness leads to difficulties in walking on toes.

name: HP_0034053
label: Decreased acid ceramidase activity
definition: Reduced activity of acid ceramidase (AC; alsoknown as N-acylsphingosine amidohydrolase; EC 3.5.1.23). The test is usually performed in cultured patient fibroblasts.

name: HP_0034054
label: Probst bundles
definition: Probst bundles (also known as longitudinal callosal fascicles) are neuroanatomical homologues to the corpus callosum and can occur in association with callosal agenesis. Probst bundles are white matter fibers that normally cross the corpus callosum but (because of the agenesis of the corpus callosum) fail to cross the midline, such that when they reach the corticoseptal boundary, they turn and run parallel to the interhemispheric fissure within the septal leaves, indenting the medial walls of the lateral ventricles.|The formation of Probst bundles is the most common structural anomaly associated with callosal dysgenesis.

name: HP_0034051
label: Hypoplastic anterior limbs of the internal capsule
definition: Underdevelopment of the frontal part (anterior crus or anterior limb) of the internal capsule.

name: HP_0034059
label: Abnormal fetal physiology
definition: Any functional anomaly of the fetus.

name: HP_0034057
label: Fetal anomaly
definition: Structural or functional abnormalities of the fetus. Note that this section comprises terms that describe abnormalities that are specific to the fetus or differ from the corresponding general terms. A term from anywhere in the Human Phenotype Ontology can be applied to a fetus if appropriate.

name: HP_0034055
label: Anti-side-chain cleavage enzyme antibody positivity
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against cytochrome P450 cholesterol side-chain cleavage enzyme (P450scc), which is encoded by CYP11A1 cytochrome P450 family 11 subfamily A member 1 (Gene ID:1583).

name: HP_0001651
label: Dextrocardia
definition: The heart is located in the right hand sided hemithorax. That is, there is a left-right reversal (or "mirror reflection") of the anatomical location of the heart in which the heart is locate on the right side instead of the left.

name: HP_0001653
label: Mitral regurgitation
definition: An abnormality of the mitral valve characterized by insufficiency or incompetence of the mitral valve resulting in retrograde leaking of blood through the mitral valve upon ventricular contraction.

name: HP_0001657
label: Prolonged QT interval
definition: Increased time between the start of the Q wave and the end of the T wave as measured by the electrocardiogram (EKG).|The QT interval represents electrical depolarization and repolarization of the left and right ventricles.

name: HP_0001654
label: Abnormal heart valve morphology
definition: Any structural abnormality of a cardiac valve.

name: HP_0001650
label: Aortic valve stenosis
definition: The presence of a stenosis (narrowing) of the aortic valve.|Aortic stenosis can lead to a pressure gradient between the left ventricle and the aorta and may result in left ventricular hypertrophy and decreased left ventricular compliance.

name: HP_0001658
label: Myocardial infarction
definition: Necrosis of the myocardium caused by an obstruction of the blood supply to the heart and often associated with chest pain, shortness of breath, palpitations, and anxiety as well as characteristic EKG findings and elevation of serum markers including creatine kinase-MB fraction and troponin.

name: HP_0001655
label: Patent foramen ovale
definition: Failure of the foramen ovale to seal postnatally, leaving a potential conduit between the left and right cardiac atria.|The foramen ovale is located in the atrial septum and is essential for proper fetal circulation. With separation from the placenta and with the first few breaths, the left atrium fills with blood returning from the lungs and closes the foramen ovale. Subsequently, during the first years of life, the foramen ovale seals shut.

name: HP_0001659
label: Aortic regurgitation
definition: An insufficiency of the aortic valve, leading to regurgitation (backward flow) of blood from the aorta into the left ventricle.

name: HP_0003398
label: Abnormal synaptic transmission at the neuromuscular junction
definition: Any abnormality of the neuromuscular junction, which is the synapse between the motor end plate of a motor neuron and the skeletal muscle fibers.

name: HP_0003393
label: Thenar muscle atrophy
definition: Wasting of thenar muscles, which are located on palm of the hand at the base of the thumb.

name: HP_0003394
label: Muscle spasm
definition: Sudden and involuntary contractions of one or more muscles.

name: HP_0003390
label: Sensory axonal neuropathy
definition: An axonal neuropathy of peripheral sensory nerves.

name: HP_0003396
label: Syringomyelia
definition: Dilated, glial-lined cavity in spinal cord. This cavity does not communicate with the central canal, and usually is between the dorsal columns unilaterally or bilaterally along the side of the cord.

name: HP_0003397
label: Generalized hypotonia due to defect at the neuromuscular junction

name: HP_0003391
label: Gowers sign
definition: A phenomenon whereby patients are not able to stand up without the use of the hands owing to weakness of the proximal muscles of the lower limbs.

name: HP_0200029
label: Vasculitis in the skin
definition: A type of vasculitis (inflammation of blood vessel walls) that affects skeletal muscle tissue.

name: HP_0200025
label: Mandibular pain
definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the mandible.

name: HP_0200028
label: Pretibial myxedema
definition: A diffuse, non-pitting edema and thickening of the skin usually on the anterior aspect of the lower legs spreading to the dorsum of the feet.

name: HP_0200022
label: Choroid plexus papilloma
definition: Choroid plexus papilloma is a histologically benign neoplasm located in the ventricular system of the choroid plexus.

name: HP_0200020
label: Corneal erosion
definition: An erosion or abrasion of the cornea's outermost layer of epithelial cells.

name: HP_0200023
label: Priapism
definition: A painful and harmful medical condition in which the erect penis doesn't return to its flaccid state, despite the absence of both physical and psychological stimulation, within four hours.

name: HP_0200021
label: Down-sloping shoulders
definition: Low set, steeply sloping shoulders.

name: HP_0200024
label: Premature chromatid separation
definition: The presence of premature sister chromatid segregation.

name: HP_0200026
label: Ocular pain
definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the eye.

name: HP_0032791
label: Focal impaired awareness cognitive seizure with anomia
definition: A focal cognitive seizure with anomia characterized by impairment of awareness at some point during the seizure.

name: HP_0032799
label: Focal impaired awareness hemiclonic seizure
definition: A focal hemiclonic seizure in which awareness is impaired at some point during the seizure.

name: HP_0032790
label: Focal impaired awareness behavior arrest seizure
definition: A focal behavior arrest seizure characterised by impaired awareness at some point during the seizure.

name: HP_0032796
label: Focal impaired awareness cognitive seizure with left-right confusion
definition: A focal cognitive seizure with left-right confusion characterized by impairment of awareness at some point during the seizure.

name: HP_0032792
label: Tonic seizure
definition: A tonic seizure is a type of motor seizure characterised by unilateral or bilateral limb stiffening or elevation, often with neck stiffening.|This term describes the initial semiology of the seizure without specifying whether the onset is focal or generalized. Thus it can be used for coding tonic seizures when the onset is not known. The tonic contraction of muscles can result in a tremor, not to be confused with a clonic phase. This term does not apply to seizures with a tonic phase followed a clonic phase, see bilateral tonic-clonic seizure.

name: HP_0032794
label: Myoclonic seizure
definition: A myoclonic seizure is a type of motor seizure characterised by sudden, brief (<100 ms) involuntary single or multiple contraction of muscles or muscle groups of variable topography (axial, proximal limb, distal). Myoclonus is less regularly repetitive and less sustained than is clonus.|This term describes the initial semiology of the seizure without specifying whether the onset is focal or generalized. Thus it can be used for coding myoclonic seizures when the onset is not known.

name: HP_0032795
label: Generalized myoclonic-tonic-clonic seizure
definition: A generalized myoclonic-tonic-clonic seizure is a type of generalized motor seizure characterised by a single or multiple jerks of limbs bilaterally, followed by tonic and clonic phases. The initial jerks can be considered to be either a brief period of clonus or myoclonus.

name: HP_0032797
label: Focal aware sensory seizure with olfactory features
definition: Seizures characterized by olfactory phenomena at onset - usually an odor, which is often unpleasant.|These seizures involve the mesial temporal or orbitofrontal regions.

name: HP_0032798
label: Focal impaired awareness cognitive seizure with neglect
definition: A focal cognitive seizure with neglect characterized by impairment of awareness at some point during the seizure.

name: HP_0032793
label: Focal impaired awareness cognitive seizure with receptive dysphasia/aphasia
definition: A focal cognitive seizure with receptive dysphasia / aphasia characterized by impairment of awareness at some point during the seizure.

name: HP_0008528
label: Long hairs growing from helix of pinna

name: HP_0008527
label: Congenital sensorineural hearing impairment
definition: A type of hearing impairment caused by an abnormal functionality of the cochlear nerve with congenital onset.

name: HP_0008523
label: Posterior helix pit
definition: Permanent indentation on the posteromedial aspect of the helix that may be sharply or indistinctly delineated.|They are usually linear to a narrow oval in shape and may be single or multiple.

name: HP_0008529
label: Absence of acoustic reflex
definition: Absence of the acoustic reflex, an involuntary contraction of the stapedius muscle that occurs in response to high-intensity sound stimuli.|Note that the acoustic reflex is also referred to as stapedius reflex, attenuation reflex, or auditory reflex.

name: HP_0001574
label: Abnormality of the integument
definition: An abnormality of the integument, which consists of the skin and the superficial fascia.|Abnormality of skin, hair, or nails.

name: HP_0001571
label: Multiple impacted teeth
definition: The presence of multiple impacted teeth.

name: HP_0001572
label: Macrodontia
definition: Increased size of the teeth, which can be defined as a mesiodistal tooth diameter (width) more than 2 SD above mean for age. Alternatively, an apparently increased maximum width of the tooth.|The standard reference has means and standard deviations by gender [Moyers et al, 1976]. Although it is easy to measure the width of teeth, and the definition is made with reference to the width of teeth, macrodontia actually means that the overall size of the tooth is increased.

name: HP_0001579
label: Primary hypercortisolism
definition: Hypercortisolemia associated with a primary defect of the adrenal gland leading to overproduction of cortisol.

name: HP_0008883
label: Mild intrauterine growth retardation
definition: Intrauterine growth retardation that is at least 2 standard deviations (SD) below average, but not as low as 3 SD, corrected for sex and gestational age.

name: HP_0008887
label: Adipose tissue loss
definition: A loss of adipose tissue.

name: HP_0002296
label: Progressive hypotrichosis
definition: Progressively reduced or lacking hair growth.

name: HP_0002290
label: Poliosis
definition: Circumscribed depigmentation of the hair of the head or the eyelashes.

name: HP_0002292
label: Frontal balding
definition: Absence of hair in the anterior midline and/or parietal areas.

name: HP_0002299
label: Brittle hair
definition: Fragile, easily breakable hair, i.e., with reduced tensile strength.|Brittle is used to describe hair which is very short because of an abnormality is in the structure of the shaft. Microscopically the ends appear fractured. Affected patients may report bits of hair on the collar or pillow. Brittle hair can be distinguished from hypotrichosis due to slow or deficient growth (e.g., due to hypotrichosis simplex) and hypotrichosis due to the hair being fine and soft where the hair just wears out too quickly (e.g., due to ectodermal dysplasia).

name: HP_0010716
label: 3-5 toe syndactyly
definition: Syndactyly with fusion of toes three to five.

name: HP_0010715
label: 2-5 toe syndactyly
definition: Syndactyly with fusion of toes two to five.

name: HP_0010713
label: 1-5 toe syndactyly
definition: Syndactyly with fusion of toes one to five (complete syndactyly of all toes of the foot).

name: HP_0010717
label: Osseous syndactyly of toes
definition: Webbing or fusion of the toes, involving soft parts and including fusion of individual bones of the toes. Bony fusions are referred to as "bony" Syndactyly if the fusion occurs in a tibial-fibular axis. Fusions of bones of the toes in a proximo-distal axis are referred to as "Symphalangism".

name: HP_0010719
label: Abnormality of hair texture
definition: An abnormality of the texture of the hair.

name: HP_0010712
label: 1-4 toe syndactyly
definition: Syndactyly with fusion of toes one to four.

name: HP_0010711
label: 1-2 toe syndactyly
definition: Syndactyly with fusion of toes one and two.

name: HP_0010714
label: 2-4 toe syndactyly
definition: Syndactyly with fusion of toes two to four.

name: HP_0010710
label: 3-5 finger syndactyly
definition: Syndactyly with fusion of fingers three to five.

name: HP_0009512
label: Triangular epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the 2nd finger
definition: A triangular appearance of the epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the 2nd finger of the hand. This epiphysis is located at the proximal end of the phalanx and is normally nearly flat.

name: HP_0009517
label: Fragmentation of the epiphysis of the middle phalanx of the 2nd finger

name: HP_0009516
label: Enlarged epiphysis of the middle phalanx of the 2nd finger

name: HP_0009519
label: Ivory epiphysis of the middle phalanx of the 2nd finger

name: HP_0009513
label: Absent epiphysis of the middle phalanx of the 2nd finger

name: HP_0009511
label: Stippling of the epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the 2nd finger
definition: The presence of abnormal punctate (speckled, dot-like) calcifications in the epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the 2nd finger.

name: HP_0009510
label: Small epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the 2nd finger
definition: Abnormally small size of the epiphysis located at the proximal end of the distal phalanx of the 2nd finger with respect to age-dependent norms.

name: HP_0009518
label: Irregular epiphysis of the middle phalanx of the 2nd finger

name: HP_0009515
label: Cone-shaped epiphysis of the middle phalanx of the 2nd finger

name: HP_0009514
label: Bracket epiphysis of the middle phalanx of the 2nd finger
definition: An abnormality of the middle phalanx of the second finger in which the epiphysis surrounds a phalangeal bone, having a bracket-like form and reaching from the proximal side of a phalanx to the distal side.

name: HP_0006711
label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia involving bones of the thorax

name: HP_0006710
label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the clavicles
definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the clavicles (collar bones).

name: HP_4000075
label: Reduced frequency of facial expressions
definition: The number of times facial expressions are produced in a given period is lower than expected given the social and cultural context.

name: HP_4000074
label: Idiosyncratic language
definition: Consistent use of an unusual way of referring to something that is idiosyncratic to the individual.

name: HP_4000078
label: Fixated interest with abnormal intensity
definition: An abnormally intense interest in a topic or object that is not atypical for the social context of the affected person.|Typical examples of fixated interests with abnormal intensity include flipping the flag on a mailbox up and down repeatedly for long periods of time, taking a fork or other such objects everywhere, repeatedly lining up toys in the same order, or repeatedly reading information about a favorite topic such as a sports team.

name: HP_4000077
label: Fixated interest with abnormal focus
definition: A fixated interest in a specific topic that is atypical for the social context of the individual, such as topics of a non-social nature like fossils or vacuum cleaners.

name: HP_4000072
label: Abnormal language feature
definition: The presence of any atypical form of expressive language.

name: HP_4000070
label: Fixated interests
definition: Highly restricted, fixated interests that are abnormal in intensity or focus (e.g., strong attachment to or preoccupation with unusual objects, excessively circumscribed or perseverative interests).

name: HP_4000076
label: Use of another person's body to communicate
definition: Moving another person's hand, body part, or body to communicate a desire, e.g. pushing or pulling someone toward a desired object or placing someone's hand on something.

name: HP_4000079
label: Sensory seeking
definition: Unusual interest in sensory aspects of the environment.

name: HP_4000073
label: Pronoun reversal
definition: Atypical language features characterized by first vs. second or third person pronoun errors such as using 'you' or 'he/she' in place of 'I'.|These errors are attested in normal toddlers' spontaneous speech, albeit at varying rates; pronouns typically emerge around 1.5 years of age and reversals are most common before 2.5 years. A higher rate of pronoun reversal may be expected of people with autism spectrum disorder.

name: HP_0009537
label: Flexion contracture of the 2nd finger
definition: Chronic loss of joint motion in the 2nd finger due to structural changes in non-bony tissue. The term camptodactyly of the 2nd finger is used if the distal and/or proximal interphalangeal joints are affected.

name: HP_0009539
label: Contracture of the metacarpophalangeal joint of the 2nd finger
definition: Chronic loss of joint motion of the metacarpophalangeal joint of the 2nd finger due to structural changes in non-bony tissue.

name: HP_0009533
label: Stippling of the epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the 2nd finger

name: HP_0009535
label: Aplasia of the 2nd finger
definition: Absent 2nd (index) finger.

name: HP_0009532
label: Small epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the 2nd finger

name: HP_0009530
label: Ivory epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the 2nd finger

name: HP_0009538
label: Contracture of the distal interphalangeal joint of the 2nd finger
definition: Chronic loss of joint motion of the distal interphalangeal joint of the 2nd finger due to structural changes in non-bony tissue.

name: HP_0009531
label: Pseudoepiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the 2nd finger
definition: A secondary ossification center in the proximal phalanx of the second finger that is distinct from the normal epiphysis that does not contribute to the longitudinal growth of a tubular bone.

name: HP_0009536
label: Short 2nd finger
definition: Hypoplasia of the second finger, also known as the index finger.

name: HP_0009534
label: Triangular epiphysis of the proximal phalanx of the 2nd finger

name: HP_0034675
label: Toe joint contracture
definition: Lack of full passive range of motion (restrictions in flexion, extension, or other movements) of a toe joint resulting from structural changes of non-bony tissues, such as muscles, tendons, ligaments, joint capsules and/or skin.

name: HP_0004362
label: Abnormal enteric ganglion morphology
definition: An abnormality of the enteric nervous system, which comprises two types of ganglia, the myenteric (Auerbach's) and submucosal (Meissner's) plexuses. The enteric nervous system functions to control gut movement, fluid exchange between the gut and its lumen, and local blood flow.

name: HP_0004364
label: Abnormal circulating nitrogen compound concentration
definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of a nitrogen compound in the blood circulation.|Ammonia (NH3), one of the most clinically important nitrogen compounds in human metabolism, is a substance containing nitrogen resulting from the catabolism of protein. It is converted to the less toxic substance urea prior to excretion in urine.

name: HP_0004369
label: Decreased circulating purine concentration
definition: Abnormally reduced concentration of a purine compound. Purine compounds are aromatic heterocyclic compounds containing a purine moiety, which is formed a pyrimidine-ring ring fused to an imidazole ring.

name: HP_0004361
label: Abnormal circulating leptin concentration
definition: An abnormal concentration of leptin in the blood.

name: HP_0004365
label: Abnormal circulating tryptophan concentration
definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of tryptophan in the blood circulation.

name: HP_0004363
label: Abnormal circulating calcium concentration
definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of calcium in the blood circulation.

name: HP_0004368
label: Increased circulating purine concentration
definition: Abnormally elevated concentration of a purine compound. Purine compounds are aromatic heterocyclic compounds containing a purine moiety, which is formed a pyrimidine-ring ring fused to an imidazole ring.

name: HP_0004360
label: Abnormality of acid-base homeostasis
definition: An abnormality of the balance or maintenance of the balance of acids and bases in bodily fluids, resulting in an abnormal pH.

name: HP_0004366
label: Abnormality of glycolysis
definition: An abnormality of glycolysis.

name: HP_0034673
label: Abnormal ankle morphology
definition: A structural anomaly of the ankle.

name: HP_0034670
label: Abnormal knee physiology
definition: A functional anomaly of the knee joint.

name: HP_0034674
label: Abnormal ankle physiology
definition: A functional anomaly of the ankle.

name: HP_0034671
label: Knee contracture
definition: Lack of full passive range of motion (restrictions in flexion, extension, or other movements) of the knee joint resulting from structural changes of non-bony tissues, such as muscles, tendons, ligaments, joint capsules and/or skin.

name: HP_0034676
label: Extension contracture of toe
definition: A type of toe joint contracture in which the joint lacks full expected flexion, so that the two bony segments on either side of their connecting joint cannot be brought together.

name: HP_0034672
label: Knee extension contracture
definition: A type of knee joint contracture in which the knee lacks full expected flexion, such that the upper and lower leg cannot be brought together.

name: HP_0009729
label: Cardiac rhabdomyoma
definition: A benign tumor of cardiac striated muscle.

name: HP_0009725
label: Bladder neoplasm
definition: The presence of a neoplasm of the urinary bladder.

name: HP_0009720
label: Adenoma sebaceum
definition: The presence of a sebaceous adenoma with origin in the sebum secreting cells of the skin.|Facial angiofibromas, also known as adenoma sebaceum, are reddish papillary lesions (fibrous skin tumors) that are found around the nose, cheeks, and chin and considered to be characteristic of tuberous sclerosis.

name: HP_0009724
label: Subungual fibromas
definition: The presence of fibromata beneath finger or toenails.

name: HP_0009721
label: Shagreen patch
definition: A plaque representing a connective-tissue nevus. Connective tissue naevi are uncommon skin lesions that occur when the deeper layers of the skin do not develop correctly or the components of these layers occur in the wrong proportion. Shagreen patches are oval-shaped and nevoid, skin-colored or occasionally pigmented, smooth or crinkled. The word shagreen refers to a type of roughened untanned leather.

name: HP_0009727
label: Achromatic retinal patches
definition: Areas of the retina lacking pigmentation. Punched out areas of chorioretinal hypopigmentation less than 1 disc diameter in size and tending to be located in the midperiphery of the retina.

name: HP_0009726
label: Renal neoplasm
definition: The presence of a neoplasm of the kidney.

name: HP_0009723
label: Abnormality of the subungual region
definition: A lesion located beneath a fingernail or toenail.

name: HP_0009722
label: Dental enamel pits
definition: The presence of small depressions in the dental enamel.

name: HP_0009728
label: Neoplasm of striated muscle
definition: A benign or malignant neoplasm (tumor) originating in striated muscle, either skeletal muscle or cardiac muscle.

name: HP_0010682
label: Elevated placental alkaline phosphatase
definition: An abnormally increased level of alkaline phosphatase, placental type in the blood.|Placental alkaline phosphatase (ALPP) is one of four distinct but related alkaline phosphatases. Entrez Gene ID 250, Uniprot P05187 (PPB1_HUMAN).

name: HP_0010681
label: Elevated intestinal alkaline phosphatase
definition: An abnormally increased level of alkaline phosphatase, intestinal type in the blood.|Intestinal alkaline phosphatase (IAP) is one of four distinct but related alkaline phosphatases. Entrez Gene ID:248, Uniprot ID: P09923 (PPBI_HUMAN).

name: HP_0010680
label: Elevated alkaline phosphatase of renal origin
definition: An abnormally increased level of kidney isoforms of alkaline phosphatase, tissue-nonspecific isozyme in the blood.

name: HP_0010684
label: Low alkaline phosphatase of bone origin
definition: An abnormally reduced level of bone isoforms of alkaline phosphatase in the blood.

name: HP_0010688
label: Low placental alkaline phosphatase
definition: An abnormally reduced level of alkaline phosphatase, placental type in the blood.

name: HP_0010685
label: Low alkaline phosphatase of renal origin
definition: An abnormally reduced level of kidney isoforms of alkaline phosphatase in the blood.

name: HP_0010689
label: Mirror image polydactyly
definition: A hand or foot with more than five digits that has a recognizable A/P axis of symmetry. The axis can lie within a normally formed or partially duplicated digit resembling a middle finger, index finger, thumb, toe, or hallux. Alternatively, the axis can be in an interdigital space with a flanking pair of digits that resemble a middle finger, index finger, thumb, toe or hallux. The most lateral digits on each side of the hand/foot typically resemble fifth fingers/toes.|Transplantation of the ZPA (zone of polarised activity) to the anterior margin of a limb bud in the chick results in mirror image duplication of limb elements (Tabin, 1991). Similarly, mirror image duplication in the forelimb of the mouse has been observed with ectopic expression of Hox b-8 (Charit6 et al, 1994). Mirror hand anomaly in humans has been shown to be due to either aberrant positioning of the ZPA or altered inductive interactions of the Shh gene resulting in impairment of the mechanism responsible for the organization and differentiation of the limb bud, rather than a primary duplication event. In other words, the primary event results in failure of the radial ray to develop. The ulnar area will then induce the differentiation of two groups of ulnar rays. Timing of this insult could play a critical role in severity of this phenotypic feature. Syndromal mirror hand is probably due to agene mutation of the Shh gene (Hersh et al, 1995). Finally, the multiple hand deformity may be explained by true duplication of the ZPA.

name: HP_0010686
label: Low alkaline phosphatase of hepatic origin
definition: An abnormally reduced level of liver isoforms of alkaline phosphatase in the blood.

name: HP_0010687
label: Low intestinal alkaline phosphatase
definition: An abnormally reduced level of alkaline phosphatase, intestinal type in the blood.

name: HP_0010683
label: Low tissue non-specific alkaline phosphatase
definition: An abnormally reduced level of alkaline phosphatase, tissue-nonspecific isozyme in the blood.

name: HP_0032143
label: Burning mouth
definition: An intense sensation of burning, scalding, or tingling feeling of the tongue or other regions of the oral mucosa.|This term implies that there is no obvious oral mucosal lesion causing the pain.

name: HP_0032141
label: Precordial pain
definition: A type of chest pain that arises in the or under the left breast and often described as throbbing, stabbing, or burning, and lasting hours or longer. The pain may arise with or after effort, and may spread to the left arm or left side of the neck.

name: HP_0032148
label: Episodic pain
definition: Intermittent pain, i.e., pain that occurs occasionally and at irregular intervals.

name: HP_0032147
label: Erythromelalgia
definition: Recurrent episodes of redness, burning pain, and warmth of the extremities following exposure to heat or exercise with symptoms predominantly involving the feet.|Warmth, ambulation, physical exercise, sitting, leg dependence and wearing shoes or gloves can provoke and aggravate symptoms while immersion in ice/cold water, uncovering affected areas, ventilation and elevation can ameliorate these symptoms. Pain attacks usually start with an itchy-like feeling and then progress to a severe burning sensation as was reported by most patients, with the durations of which ranging from several minutes to hours and even days. Erythromelalgia can be a Mendelian trait or can be triggered by polycythemia vera, lymphoproliferative disorders, hypertension, and hyperviscosity.

name: HP_0032144
label: Coffee ground vomitus
definition: Vomit that has the appearance of coffee grounds, which occurs due to the presence of coagulated blood in the vomit.

name: HP_0032149
label: Breakthrough pain
definition: A episode of severe pain that breaks through (i.e., temporarily exacerbates) a period of persistent pain.

name: HP_0032140
label: Decreased specific antibody response to vaccination
definition: A reduced ability to synthesize postvaccination antibodies against toxoids and polysaccharides in vaccines, as measured by antibody titer determination following vaccination.

name: HP_0032142
label: Fetor hepaticus
definition: Fetor hepaticus is the characteristic breath of patients with severe parenchymal liver disease, which has been said to resemble the odor of a mixture of rotten eggs and garlic.

name: HP_0032146
label: HbC hemoglobin
definition: Presence of an abnormal type of hemoglobin characterized by the subsitution of a glutamic acid residue at position 7 following the initial methionine residue by a lysine (6GAG>6AAG). The presence of HbC can be determined by hemoglobin electrophoresis.

name: HP_0032145
label: Sural nerve atrophy
definition: Wasting of the sural nerve, a sensory nerve in the calf region of the leg.

name: HP_0012324
label: Myeloid leukemia
definition: A leukemia that originates from a myeloid cell, that is the blood forming cells of the bone marrow.

name: HP_0012326
label: Abnormal celiac artery morphology
definition: An anomaly of the celiac artery.|The celiac artery (celiac trunk or truncus coeliacus) is the first major branch of the abdominal aorta.

name: HP_0012322
label: Perifolliculitis
definition: Inflammation surrounding hair follicles.

name: HP_0012321
label: D-2-hydroxyglutaric aciduria
definition: An increased concentration of 2-hydroxyglutaric acid in the urine.

name: HP_0012328
label: Cementoma
definition: An odontogenic tumor of the cementum of tooth.

name: HP_0012320
label: Absent pigmentation of the limbs
definition: Lack of skin pigmentation (coloring) of the arms and legs.

name: HP_0012327
label: Celiac artery compression
definition: Compression of the celiac artery.|This feature may be characterized by abdominal pain related to compression of the celiac artery by fibers of the median arcuate ligament.

name: HP_0012323
label: Sleep myoclonus
definition: Myoclonus that occurs during the initial phases of sleep.

name: HP_0012325
label: Chronic myelomonocytic leukemia
definition: A myelodysplastic/myeloproliferative neoplasm which is characterized by persistent monocytosis, absence of a Philadelphia chromosome and BCR/ABL fusion gene, fewer than 20 percent blasts in the bone marrow and blood, myelodysplasia, and absence of PDGFRA or PDGFRB rearrangement.

name: HP_0012329
label: Tufted angioma
definition: A vascular tumor of the skin and subcutaneous tissues and characterized by slow angiomatous proliferation.

name: HP_0033903
label: Arcuate artery endoarterial hypercellularity
definition: Proliferation of endothelial cells (increased number of cells) of the lining (endothelium) of the arcuate arteries of the kidney.

name: HP_0033902
label: Arcuate artery endotheliosis
definition: Enlargement of endothelial cells of the arcuate arteries of the kidney because of cytoplasmic swelling.

name: HP_0033909
label: Arcuate vein medial hypertrophy
definition: Increased thickness of middle layer of the arcuate veins of the kidney.

name: HP_0033904
label: Renal arteriole intima/media hyalinosis
definition: Accumulation of amorphous, eosinophilic, glassy, periodic acid-Schiff (PAS)-positive, silver-negative material (hyalinosis) in the inner or middle layer of the renal arterioles. This feature may be accompanied by hypertrophy of the media and intima fibrosis.

name: HP_0033907
label: Renal arteriole intima/media arteriolosclerosis
definition: Thickening of the intima of renal arterioles with fibrosis and/or duplication of the elastic lamina.

name: HP_0033905
label: Arcuate artery intima/media arteriosclerosis
definition: Thickening of the intima of the arcuate arteries of the kidney with fibrosis and/or duplication of the elastic lamina.

name: HP_0033906
label: Renal intimal/medial arteriolitis
definition: Inflammation of an arteriole of the kidney, which may involve only the intma or can be transmural.

name: HP_0033900
label: Renal arteriole intima/media amyloidosis
definition: Amorphous extracellular substance in the inner or middle layer of renal arterioles. Amyloidosis stains Congo-red positive with typically an apple green birerfingence on polarization microscopy, and 8-12 nm fibrils on electron microscopy.

name: HP_0033901
label: Abnormal arcuate artery endothelium morphology
definition: Any structural anomaly of the lining (endothelium) of the arcuate arteries of the kidney.

name: HP_0033908
label: Renal arteriole medial atrophy
definition: Atrophy (wasting, decreased thickness) of of the middle layer of the arterioles of the kidney.

name: HP_0500248
label: Increased CSF alpha-aminobutyrate concentration
definition: Concentration of alpha-aminobutyrate in the cerebrospinal fluid above the upper limit of normal.

name: HP_0500246
label: Increased CSF citrulline concentration
definition: Abnormally increased levels of citrulline in cerebrospinal fluid.

name: HP_0500242
label: Increased CSF homocarnosine concentration
definition: Abnormally increased levels of homocarnosine in cerebrospinal fluid.

name: HP_0500249
label: Abnormal circulating ethanolamine concentration
definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of ethanolamine in circulation.

name: HP_0500240
label: Abnormal CSF carnosine concentration
definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of carnosine in the cerebrospinal fluid.

name: HP_0500247
label: Abnormal CSF alpha-aminobutyrate concentration
definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of alpha-aminobutyrate in the cerebrospinal fluid.

name: HP_0500241
label: Abnormal CSF homocarnosine concentration
definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of homocarnosine in the cerebrospinal fluid.

name: HP_0500243
label: Abnormal CSF ornithine concentration
definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of ornithine in the cerebrospinal fluid.

name: HP_0500245
label: Abnormal CSF citrulline concentration
definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of citrulline in the cerebrospinal fluid.

name: HP_0500244
label: Increased CSF ornithine concentration
definition: Abnormally increased levels of ornithine in cerebrospinal fluid.

name: HP_0010705
label: 4-5 finger syndactyly
definition: Syndactyly with fusion of fingers four and five.

name: HP_0010701
label: Abnormal immunoglobulin level
definition: An abnormal deviation from normal levels of immunoglobulins in blood.|'has part' some (amount and ('inheres in' some (IMR_0002090 and ('part of' some blood))) and ('has modifier' some abnormal))

name: HP_0010707
label: 1-4 finger syndactyly
definition: Syndactyly with fusion of fingers one to four.

name: HP_0010706
label: 1-3 finger syndactyly
definition: Syndactyly with fusion of fingers one to three.

name: HP_0010704
label: 1-2 finger syndactyly
definition: Syndactyly with fusion of fingers one and two.

name: HP_0010702
label: Increased circulating antibody level
definition: An increased level of gamma globulin (immunoglobulin) in the blood.|In humans, immunoglobulins comprise the five antibody isotypes IgA, IgD, IgE, IgG and IgM.

name: HP_0010709
label: 2-4 finger syndactyly
definition: Syndactyly with fusion of the fingers two to four.

name: HP_0010708
label: 1-5 finger syndactyly
definition: Syndactyly with fusion of fingers one to five (complete syndactyly of all fingers of the hand).

name: HP_0025376
label: Hyperglutaminuria
definition: An increased concentration of glutamine in the urine.

name: HP_0025372
label: Loud snoring
definition: Snoring at a particularly loud or abnormally high volume.|The NREM stages of sleep are not skipped.

name: HP_0025371
label: Delayed ossification of the sacrum
definition: Formation of the sacrum bone tissue occurs later than age-adjusted norms.

name: HP_0025043
label: Enlarged mesenteric lymph node
definition: Increase in size of one or more mesenteric lymph nodes.|Mesenteric lymph nodes measured by CT as being larger than 10 mm are considered enlarged.

name: HP_0025379
label: Anti-thyroid peroxidase antibody positivity
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against thyroid peroxidase.|Thyroid peroxidase (TPO) antibody positivity is found in most patients with chronic lymphocytic thyroiditis (Hashimoto disease) and over half of patients with Graves disease.

name: HP_0025375
label: Orthotopic os odontoideum
definition: Os odontoideum is classified into two anatomic types (orthotopic and dystopic). Os odontoideum is defined as an ossicle that consists of smooth and separate caudal portions of the odontoid process.With dystopic os odontoideum, the ossicle is located near the basion or is fused with the clivus.

name: HP_0025374
label: Duplicated odontoid process
definition: The presence of two distinct odontoid processes. The odontoid process, also known as the dens of the axis, is a protuberance of the C2 vertebral body around which the first vertebra rotates.|The odontoid process forms from different ossification centers. Two centers normally appear on each side of the midline around the fifth or sixth month of fetal life. These two centers usually fuse by one year of age. When there is a delay in fusion, a longitudinal midline cleft may be seen. Duplication of the odontoid process most likely is the result of a lack of fusion of these two centers of ossification [from PMID:9367321].

name: HP_0025373
label: Interictal EEG abnormality
definition: Interictal refers to a period of time between epileptic seizures. Electroencephalographic (EEG) patterns are important in the differential diagnosis of epilepsy, and the EEG is almost always abnormal during a seizure. Some persons with seizures may show EEG abnormalities between seizures, while others do not. In some cases, multiple interictal EEGs must be recorded before an abnormality is observed. In most cases the electrographic pattern of seizure onset is completely different from the activity recorded during interictal discharge.

name: HP_0025370
label: Abnormal ossification of the sacrum
definition: Abnormal bone tissue formation (ossification) affecting the sacrum.

name: HP_0025377
label: Triggered by exertion
definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by exertion or physical exercise.|For convenience, several HPO terms exist with the phrase 'Exercise-induced' in their label. This is meant to be logically equvalent to the combination of the basis term and this modifier.

name: HP_0000275
label: Narrow face
definition: Bizygomatic (upper face) and bigonial (lower face) width are both more than 2 standard deviations below the mean (objective); or, an apparent reduction in the width of the upper and lower face (subjective).|Objective measurement of the upper facial width is made with spreading calipers. The tips of the calipers are passed over the zygomatic arches until the maximum width is determined. Objective measurement of the lower faces is made with spreading calipers, with the tips firmly pressed against the inferomedial surface of the angle of the mandible.

name: HP_0000271
label: Abnormality of the face
definition: An abnormality of the face.

name: HP_0000277
label: Abnormal mandible morphology
definition: Any abnormality of the mandible, the bone of the lower jaw.

name: HP_0000272
label: Malar flattening
definition: Underdevelopment of the malar prominence of the jugal bone (zygomatic bone in mammals), appreciated in profile, frontal view, and/or by palpation.|The malar process is the most medial and superior portion of the bony midface, articulating with the maxilla and temporal and sphenoid bones, contiguous with the lateral boundary of the nasal bridge. The term malar hypoplasia is no longer preferred because surface examination cannot distinguish hypoplasia from hypotrophy.

name: HP_0000276
label: Long face
definition: Facial height (length) is more than 2 standard deviations above the mean (objective); or, an apparent increase in the height (length) of the face (subjective).|Objective measurement of the face height is made with sliding calipers from the nasion, just above the depth of the nasal root, to the gnathion, the inferior border of the mandible, both in the midline. Note that long face is distinct from narrow face.

name: HP_0000274
label: Small face
definition: A face that is short and narrow.|This term represents a combination of two terms, short face and narrow face.

name: HP_0000270
label: Delayed cranial suture closure
definition: Infants normally have two fontanels at birth, the diamond-shaped anterior fontanelle at the junction of the coronal and sagittal sutures, and the posterior fontanelle at the intersection of the occipital and parietal bones. The posterior fontanelle usually closes by the 8th week of life, and the anterior fontanel closes by the 18th month of life on average. This term applies if there is delay of closure of the fontanelles beyond the normal age.

name: HP_0000278
label: Retrognathia
definition: An abnormality in which the mandible is mislocalised posteriorly.

name: HP_0025046
label: Reduced brain lactate level by MRS
definition: A decrease in the level of lactate in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).

name: HP_0025049
label: Abnormal brain creatine level by MRS
definition: A deviation from normal in the level of creatine in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).

name: HP_0025041
label: Thalamic calcification
definition: Calcium deposition in the thalamus.

name: HP_0025048
label: Reduced brain choline level by MRS
definition: An decrease in the level of choline-containing compounds in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).

name: HP_0025040
label: Thalamic edema
definition: Swelling within the thalamus due to the accumulation of fluid.

name: HP_0025045
label: Abnormal brain lactate level by MRS
definition: A deviation from normal of the level of lactate in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).

name: HP_0025042
label: Abnormality of mesenteric lymph nodes
definition: A morphological anomaly of lymph nodes in the mesenteric root or throughout the mesentery.

name: HP_0025044
label: Lung abscess
definition: A circumscribed area of pus or necrotic debris in lung parenchyma, which leads to a cavity, and after formation of bronchopulmonary fistula, can manifest as an air-fluid level inside the cavity.

name: HP_0025047
label: Abnormal brain choline level by MRS
definition: A deviation from normal in the level of choline-containing compounds in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).

name: HP_0005964
label: Intermittent hypothermia
definition: Episodes of reduced body termperature.

name: HP_0005961
label: Hypoargininemia
definition: A decreased concentration of arginine in the blood.

name: HP_0005968
label: Temperature instability
definition: Disordered thermoregulation characterized by an impaired ability to maintain a balance between heat production and heat loss, with resulting instability of body temperature.

name: HP_0032319
label: Health status
definition: Health status of a family member with respect to the disease being investigated in a proband.

name: HP_0032312
label: Decreased circulating globulin level
definition: An abnormally reduced concentration of globulins in the blood.

name: HP_0032313
label: Frontotemporal hypertrichosis
definition: Excessive, increased hair growth located in the region of the forehead and temple.

name: HP_0032318
label: Family history of heart disease
definition: A close blood relative had heart disease.

name: HP_0032314
label: Abnormal areolar morphology
definition: An abnormal appearance or structure of the ring of pigmented skin that surrounds the nipple.

name: HP_0032315
label: Areolar fullness
definition: The areola (ring of pigmented skin surrounding the nipple) is filled out so as to produce a rounded shape.

name: HP_0032316
label: Family history
definition: Information about close relatives of an individual who is the proband of a study or who is being investigated with the goal of identifying a medical diagnosis. Usually, the family history includes information from three generations of relatives, including children, brothers and sisters, parents, aunts and uncles, nieces and nephews, grandparents, and cousins.|This subontology is intended to help record summary information about family members if only a limited amount of information is available or required.

name: HP_0032311
label: Increased circulating globulin level
definition: An abnormally elevated concentration of globulins in the blood.

name: HP_0032317
label: Family history of cancer
definition: A close blood relative had cancer.

name: HP_0032310
label: Granulocytosis
definition: An increased count of granulocytes in the peripheral blood circulation.

name: HP_0005411
label: Chronic intestinal candidiasis
definition: Persistent overgrowth of Candida albicans in the gastrointestinal tract.

name: HP_0002056
label: Abnormality of the glabella
definition: An abnormality of the glabella.

name: HP_0005413
label: Increased alpha-globulin
definition: An abnormally increased level of circulating alpha-globulin. Alpha globulins are a group of serum proteins defined by their mobility on serum electrophoresis. The alpha1-protein fraction is comprised of alpha1-antitrypsin, thyroid-binding globulin, and transcortin. Ceruloplasmin, alpha2-macroglobulin, and haptoglobin contribute to the alpha2-protein band. The alpha2 component is increased as an acute-phase reactant.

name: HP_0005415
label: Decreased proportion of CD8-positive T cells
definition: A decreased proportion of circulating CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cells relative to total number of T cells.

name: HP_0005416
label: Decreased circulating complement factor B concentration
definition: Concentration of the complement component factor B in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.

name: HP_0005419
label: Decreased T cell activation
definition: Decreased or impaired activation of T cells in response to a mitogen, cytokine, chemokine, cellular ligand, or an antigen for which it is specific.

name: HP_0010299
label: Abnormal dentin morphology
definition: Any abnormality of dentin.|Dentin is a calcified tissue of teeth that is covered by enamel on the crown and cementum on the root and surrounds the entire pulp.

name: HP_0010295
label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the tongue
definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the tongue.

name: HP_0010290
label: Short hard palate
definition: Distance between the labial point of the incisive papilla to the midline junction of the hard and soft palate more than 2 SD below the mean (objective) or apparently decreased length of the hard palate (subjective).|Objective measurement of the hard palate requires special instrumentation [Hall JG, Froster-Iskenius UG, Allanson JE, Gripp K, Slavotinek A. 2006. Handbook of Normal Physical Measurements. 2nd edition. Oxford Medical, publishers]. A short hard palate may be associated with velopharyngeal incompetence.

name: HP_0010292
label: Absent uvula
definition: Lack of the uvula.|Sometimes accompanies a Submucous cleft palate, but this should be coded separately.

name: HP_0010298
label: Smooth tongue
definition: Glossy appearance of the entire tongue surface.|This is due to reduction in number and/or size of the filiform papillae. A geographic tongue has localized areas of smoothening, but not sufficient to warrant use of the term Smooth tongue.

name: HP_0010294
label: Palate fistula
definition: A fistula which connects the oral cavity and the pharyngeal area via the aspects of the soft palate.

name: HP_0010293
label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the uvula
definition: Underdevelopment or absence of the uvula.

name: HP_0010291
label: Prominent palatine ridges
definition: Increased size and/or number of soft tissue folds on the palatal side of the maxillary alveolar ridge.|Soft tissue folds are typically present on the lateral sides of the palate, especially anteriorly.

name: HP_0009584
label: Osteolytic defects of the proximal phalanx of the 2nd finger
definition: Dissolution or degeneration of bone tissue of the proximal phalanx of the 2nd finger.

name: HP_0010296
label: Ankyloglossia
definition: Short or anteriorly attached lingual frenulum, associated with limited mobility of the tongue.|The anterior third of the tongue is usually free or is partially attached to the floor of the mouth by the lingual frenulum. There is a spectrum ranging from fusion of the tongue to the floor of the mouth (ankyloglossia inferiorum) to a lingual frenulum that is short or anchored toward the tip of the tongue (sometimes called tongue tie). Ankyloglossia may be associated with a mild indentation of the tip of the tongue, which should not be coded as a Bifid tongue.

name: HP_0010297
label: Bifid tongue
definition: Tongue with a median apical indentation or fork.|Bifid tongue can be associated with ankyloglossia, but this should be assessed and coded separately. Small indentations of the tip of the tongue should not be coded as a bifid tongue.

name: HP_0034214
label: Fetal intraventricular hemorrhage without ventriculomegaly
definition: A type of fetal intraventricular hemorrhage characterized by clear hemorrhage spillover to the ventricles filling less than 50% of the lateral ventricle and without ventriculomegaly of greater than 15 mm in the transverse diameter of the lateral ventricular atrium.

name: HP_0034213
label: Fetal posterior fossa hemorrhage
definition: A type of fetal intracranial hemorrhage that occurs in the posterior cranial fossa, which is the part of the cranial cavity that is located between the foramen magnum and tentorium cerebelli and contains the brainstem and cerebellum.

name: HP_0034211
label: Fetal cerebral parenchymal hemorrhage
definition: A type of fetal intracranial hemorrhage with bleeding into the parenchyma (tissue) of the brain.

name: HP_0034216
label: Fetal cerebellar vermis hemorrhage
definition: A type of fetal intracranial hemorrhage that occurs in the vermis of the cerebellum.

name: HP_0034218
label: Fetal intraventricular hemorrhage with ventriculomegaly
definition: A type of fetal intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH) characterized by spillover to ventricles with flooding of 50% or more of one or both lateral ventricles accrued accompanying ventriculomegaly, but with no apparent brain parenchymal injury. This type of IVH may be defined as a diameter exceeding 15 mm in the transverse diameter of the lateral ventricular atrium as visualiuzed by prenatal sonography.

name: HP_0034219
label: Fetal intraventricular hemorrhage with periventricular hemorrhage
definition: A type of fetal intraventricular hemorrhage that additionally includes hemorrhage in a large part of the periventricular parenchyma.

name: HP_0034215
label: Fetal cerebellar hemisphere hemorrhage
definition: A type of fetal intracranial hemorrhage that occurs in the hemisphere of the cerebellum.

name: HP_0034210
label: Fetal intraventricular hemorrhage
definition: A type of fetal intracranial hemorrhage with bleeding into the ventricular system of the brain.|The evolution of the ultrasonographic pattern of intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH) is that fresh blood clots appear as homogeneously echogenic areas, separate from the choroid plexus. Over the course of several weeks some blood clots develop a complex appearance, with an external echogenic lining and an internal sonolucent core.

name: HP_0034212
label: Fetal extra-axial hemorrhage
definition: A type of fetal intracranial hemorrhage with bleeding that occurs within the skull but outside of the brain tissue itself (into the epidural, subdural, or arachnoid space).

name: HP_0034217
label: Sonographic non-visualized fetal bladder
definition: Inability to visualize the fetal bladder on targeted prenatal sonography examination. The fetal bladder can be visualized with sonography as a midline, fluid-filled structure in the pelvis as early as 10-12 weeks of gestation. The normal fetus voids at least once an hour but never completely empties the urinary bladder. The fetal bladdder should be consistently imaged after 13 weeks of gestation.

name: HP_0000586
label: Shallow orbits
definition: Reduced depth of the orbits associated with prominent-appearing ocular globes.

name: HP_0000585
label: Band keratopathy
definition: An abnormality of the cornea characterized by the deposition of calcium in a band across the central cornea, leading to decreased vision, foreign body sensation, and ocular irritation.

name: HP_0000581
label: Blepharophimosis
definition: A fixed reduction in the vertical distance between the upper and lower eyelids with short palpebral fissures.|When the palpebral fissures are severely shortened, they cannot be widely separated, actively or passively. Blepharophimosis is an acknowledged bundled term (short vertical and horizontal distance). When palpebral fissures are severely shortened, they cannot be widely separated, actively or passively. Ptosis is the term to be used when the reduction in eyelid opening is not fixed but can be increased actively or passively. Blepharophimosis is often associated with Epicanthus inversus.

name: HP_0000582
label: Upslanted palpebral fissure
definition: The palpebral fissure inclination is more than two standard deviations above the mean for age (objective); or, the inclination of the palpebral fissure is greater than typical for age.

name: HP_0000589
label: Coloboma
definition: A developmental defect characterized by a cleft of some portion of the eye or ocular adnexa.

name: HP_0000588
label: Optic disc coloboma
definition: A cleft of the optic nerve that extends inferiorly.|A congenital, unilateral or bilateral congenital condition caused by incomplete closure of the embryonic fissure.

name: HP_0002057
label: Prominent glabella
definition: Forward protrusion of the glabella.|The glabella is the area of the forehead in the midline between the supraorbital ridges, just above the nasal root.

name: HP_0000580
label: Pigmentary retinopathy
definition: An abnormality of the retina characterized by pigment deposition. It is typically associated with migration and proliferation of macrophages or retinal pigment epithelial cells into the retina; melanin from these cells causes the pigmentary changes. Pigmentary retinopathy is a common final pathway of many retinal conditions and is often associated with visual loss.

name: HP_0000587
label: Abnormal optic nerve morphology
definition: Abnormality of the optic nerve.|The optic nerve, which is also known as cranial nerve II, transmits visual information from the retina to the brain. The term 'optic disc' is frequently used to describe the portion of the optic nerve clinically visible on fundoscopic examination.

name: HP_0000194
label: Open mouth
definition: A facial appearance characterized by a permanently or nearly permanently opened mouth.

name: HP_0000196
label: Lower lip pit
definition: Depression located on the vermilion of the lower lip, usually paramedian.|A lip pit may be connected by a fistula to mucous minor salivary glands in the lower lip. In addition, a lip pit may on occasion be seen with a surrounding tissue elevation (mound). Pits located at the labial commisure (cheilon) are distinct from lip pits (see Commissural pit).

name: HP_0000197
label: Abnormal parotid gland morphology
definition: Any abnormality of the parotid glands, which are the salivary glands that are located in the subcutaneous tissues of the face overlying the mandibular ramus and anterior and inferior to the external ear.

name: HP_0000191
label: Accessory oral frenulum
definition: Extra fold of tissue extending from the alveolar ridge to the inner surface of the upper or lower lip.|This finding is assessed by gently retracting the oral mucosa from the alveolar ridge. Typically there is a single maxillary and a single mandibular frenulum located in the midline between the two central incisors. Abnormalities of the alveolar ridges may accompany accessory frenula, but these should be assessed separately.

name: HP_0000190
label: Abnormal oral frenulum morphology
definition: An abnormality of the lingual frenulum, that is of the small fold of mucous membrane that attaches the tongue to the floor of the mouth, or the presence of accessory frenula in the oral cavity.|A frenulum is a small frenum. There are several frena that are usually present in a normal oral cavity, most notably the maxillary labial frenum, the mandibular labial frenum, and the lingual frenum.

name: HP_0000193
label: Bifid uvula
definition: Uvula separated into two parts most easily seen at the tip.

name: HP_0002055
label: Curved linear dimple below the lower lip

name: HP_0006562
label: Viral hepatitis
definition: Inflammation of the liver due to infection with a virus.

name: HP_0034182
label: Segmental hypoplasia of liver
definition: Anatomically the liver is divided into right and left lobes based on the attachment of its peritoneal ligaments. This term refers to a developmental anomaly characterzied by the underdevelopment of one of the lobes of the liver. This is a rare and usually asymptomatic anomaly that can be detected incidentally on cross sectional imaging with computed tomography or magnetic resonance imaging.

name: HP_0034183
label: Spastic triplegia
definition: Spastic weakness found in both lower extremities and one upper extremity.

name: HP_0034188
label: Midline liver
definition: Position of the liver across the middle of the body instead of being in its normal position to the right of the stomach.

name: HP_0034184
label: Increased insulin like growth factor binding protein acid labile subunit concentration
definition: An abnormally elevated concentration of insulin like growth factor binding protein acid labile subunit level in the blood circulation.

name: HP_0034185
label: Median pseudocleft lip
definition: A type of mild median cleft lip in which the central tubercle of the upper lip is replaced by a mucosal cleft in the midline.|See Figure 1 of PMID:25535458.

name: HP_0034187
label: Clavicular pseudarthrosis
definition: A developmental defect in a the clavicule leading to bending and pathologic fracture, with inability to form a normal bony callus with subsequent fibrous nonunion, leading to the pseudarthrosis (or false joint).

name: HP_0034180
label: Fusion of the caudate and putamen
definition: Abnormal joined appearance of the caudate and putamen with an absence of the anterior limb of the internal capsule.|The putamen, combined with the globus pallidus, forms the lentiform nucleus; and with the caudate nucleus, it shapes the striatum, which is a subcortical structure that forms the basal ganglia.

name: HP_0034186
label: Patella alta
definition: Patella alta is a patella that rides abnormally high in relation to the femur, the femoral trochlea, or the tibia, with decreased bony stability requiring increased knee flexion angles to engage the trochlea.|An abnormally high patella may therefore insufficiently engage the proximal trochlea groove both in extension and in the early phase of knee flexion - making it one of the potential risk factors for patellar instability. Accordingly, patella alta is present in 30% of patients with recurrent patellar dislocation.

name: HP_0034189
label: Anti-thyroid-stimulating hormone receptor antibody positivity
definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against thyroid-stimulating hormone.

name: HP_0034181
label: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the liver
definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the liver.

name: HP_0002059
label: Cerebral atrophy
definition: Atrophy (wasting, decrease in size of cells or tissue) affecting the cerebrum.|Atrophy may be progressive over time.

name: HP_0002058
label: Myopathic facies
definition: A facial appearance characteristic of myopathic conditions. The face appears expressionless with sunken cheeks, bilateral ptosis, and inability to elevate the corners of the mouth, due to muscle weakness.

name: HP_0009582
label: Bullet-shaped proximal phalanx of the 2nd finger
definition: Bullet-shaped phalanx refers to a short and wide phalanx that tapers distally. Bullet-shaped phalanges lack the normal diaphyseal constriction. This term is used if the proximal phalanx of the 2nd finger is affected.

name: HP_0009587
label: Triangular shaped proximal phalanx of the 2nd finger
definition: Triangular shaped proximal phalanx of the 2nd finger. A triangular or so called delta shaped phalanx is a typical result after a bracket epiphysis of the affected phalanx.

name: HP_0009583
label: Curved proximal phalanx of the 2nd finger
definition: Curved appearance of the proximal phalanx of the 2nd finger.

name: HP_0009585
label: Patchy sclerosis of the proximal phalanx of the 2nd finger
definition: Uneven (irregular) increase in bone density of the proximal phalanx of the second finger.

name: HP_0009586
label: Symphalangism affecting the proximal phalanx of the 2nd finger
